info.title: Agent Cookie workspace
info.description:
The workspace HTTP API that @agent-cookie/sdk wraps, for clients in any language. Generated from @agent-cookie/contract
(src/endpoints.ts and the TypeScript types) by packages/contract/scripts/openapi.ts; do not edit by hand.

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <key>`: the key from POST /agents/register, or the owner key. Each operation
names the key roles it accepts. Every error is an ErrorBody `{ error: { code, message } }`; messages never name a field
the caller may not know, and every 404 is identical. Objects are open: a later contract version may add optional
properties, so ignore the ones you do not know. Prices are integer cents of USD.

bearer.description: The agent's key (shown once by POST /agents/register; keep it in AGENT_COOKIE_KEY, never in chat, logs or commits) or the user's owner key. The key's role decides which operations it may call.

message.description: Human-readable, passed through to the user verbatim (sold-out warnings, escalation reasons).

receipts.description: Receipts written during this accept (who read which field for which purpose) — for telling the user.

authorization.description: Additive (lane D, A21): the payment authorization the workspace made for this accept, when payment is on and the card holds a payment_method token. The RESULT only (id, amount, status) — never the token or a provider reference. An authorization is not an order: `status` above still says what the store did.

AcceptResult.description: Response of POST /personal/quotes/:id/accept.  ordered  = checkout completed; `orderId` set.  handoff  = UCP `requires_escalation`, or the store refusing to complete without the buyer signed in             (INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS / AUTH_REQUIRED; A17, confirmed): the user pays on the merchant's page;             `continueUrl` is mandatory for UCP quotes.             This is the DEFAULT outcome — UCP stores mostly report native_checkout=false, so "can pay for             you" is never promised.  blocked  = policy refused a step (e.g. shipping_address → PURPOSE_MISMATCH); `code` set, nothing ordered.  failed   = upstream (ucp / Photon / payment provider) failed; `code` = UPSTREAM_ERROR; `continueUrl`             included whenever the upstream gave one. Never dressed up as success (A18).

kind.description: Additive (2026-10-18): "dreaming" on events the periodic Dreaming job writes; "search" on the `ucp.search` event of an intent (docs/commerce-analytics-plan.md Phase 0); absent on request events.

stats.description: Dreaming, search and rank events only: counts, never field values.

ActivityEvent.description: One activity row. Never contains field values.

ActivityResponse.description: GET /owner/activity. Newest first; never field values.

field.description: A Field name, or the unknown name a merchant sent (kept as its own inferred record, A11).

AgentContribution.description: The caller's own contribution record as stored (POST /agent/contributions, POST /assistant/contributions); never the user's id.

AssistantContext.description: GET /assistant/context: what a linked assistant may know, as VALUES (it acts for the user) but without provenance. `fields` = auto.assistant fields that have a value; `unknown` = auto.assistant fields without one (ask only when the task needs them); `writable` = write.assistant. A call that serves values writes a receipt (purpose "assist", field names only), except when the session's last assist receipt named the same fields under the same policy less than an hour ago (a chat reads its context on every message; every receipt is a git commit).

AssistantContributionRequest.description: POST /assistant/contributions body: AssistantContributionInput plus the optional session, which must be the assistant's own (else 404).

conversationId.description: Opaque, at most 128 bytes; never a phone number or email.

snippet.description: The user's own words, 1–EVIDENCE_SNIPPET_MAX characters, no contact or payment data.

AssistantEvidence.description: The evidence of an assistant's contribution: both fields required. Named (A59) so the JSON Schema keeps them required; the same shape as Required<Pick<ContributionEvidence, "conversationId" | "snippet">>.

quoted.description: Of those, intents that received at least one quote.

accepted.description: Of those, intents whose user accepted a quote.

completed.description: Of those, accepted intents whose result reached a terminal success (ordered or handoff).

questionsSkipped.description: Sum of FunnelRow.questionsSkipped over those intents.

AssistantStats.description: GET /assistant/stats: counts over the intents the calling assistant created (bring-your-own-agent plan §5).

evidenceSources.description: As CardField.evidenceSources: independent conversations / intents behind this value (lane C fills it).

superseded.description: Values that used to be on the card and were replaced by a newer qualified value. History, not card.

decayed.description: Additive (Dreaming, 2026-10-18; RulesApi.mergeCard fills it, lane C): fields that, at `now`, are held back purely by age — a card value downgraded to medium because lastSupportedAt is older than 180 days although it has two or more sources, or a field that left the card because its last support is older than 365 days. Pure: the same contributions and `now` give the same list. For logs only; never values.

source.description: Set by the workspace on GET /personal/card (additive, B20): "sample" whenever a card value rests on Sample seed data. RulesApi.mergeCard does not set it.

Card.description: Return shape of RulesApi.mergeCard and of GET /personal/card.

evidenceSources.description: Learned values (B49, lane C fills it): canonical independent sources RulesApi.mergeCard counted for this value — distinct conversations / intents from evidence, not writers. `sources` stays the writers' agentIds.

Category.description: pharmacy and hotel were cut on 2026-10-17; they come back after the hackathon, not before. "retail" (2026-10-17, human direction: search is driven by the user's own words): the category of UCP store proxies (`ucp:<domain>`), whatever they sell. Same policy as "shoe" (policy.ts). "shoe" stays for registered merchants that declared it.

offsetMs.description: Milliseconds added to the server clock; at most ten years either way.

models.description: Which models produced a learned contribution (B60). Provenance only, never authority.

ContributionEvidence.description: Where a learned contribution came from (additive, 2026-10-17). `snippet` is at most EVIDENCE_SNIPPET_MAX characters of the user's OWN words (never another party's), kept so the user can see why something was learned; the conversation it came from is not kept.

stored.description: The basis the workspace stored it with ("inferred" when the policy does not let the caller write that field).

DataSource.description: Where a response's data comes from (lane B, B20). "sample" = Sample seed/demo data (fixtures); "fixture" = recorded upstream responses replayed (AGENT_COOKIE_UCP=fixture); "live" = real upstream calls or real agent input. Clients label "sample" and "fixture" data as Sample and never present them as live inventory or identity.

DreamingRun.description: Response of POST /owner/dreaming/run (and what each scheduled run computes).

learned.description: Contributions written from observed conversations in this run.

promoted.description: Card entries (field + value) that were not on the card at the previous run and are now.

decayed.description: Fields in Card.decayed at this run's `now`.

archived.description: Contribution lines moved to archive/ by compaction.

continueUrl.description: Additive (A59, as UpstreamError.toBody sends it): UPSTREAM_ERROR only, the upstream's continue_url when it gave one.

ErrorBody.description: Wire shape of every error response. Never includes field names the caller is not allowed to know.

ErrorCode.description: Error codes and their HTTP status: AUTH_REQUIRED 401, SCOPE_DENIED 403, GRANT_EXPIRED 403, GRANT_REVOKED 403, PURPOSE_MISMATCH 403, NOT_FOUND 404, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT 409, LINK_NOT_PENDING 409, MISSING_FIELD 422, UPSTREAM_ERROR 502, JAR_LOCKED 403, AUTHORIZATION_USED 403, OVER_BUDGET 403.

EvidenceModels.description: B60: the model ids behind a learned value — `gate`, the classifier that decided the turn may be learned from (e.g. Jev Decisions), and `extractor`, the model that produced the value. Each is an opaque model id of at most EVIDENCE_MODEL_ID_MAX characters from [A-Za-z0-9._:/@-]. Shown in GET /personal/learned; persisted on the contribution's memory-repo line as the open keys `gate:` / `extractor:`; RulesApi.mergeCard ignores it.

ExperimentArm.description: The arm of a holdout experiment an intent is in. Assigned once, when the intent is created, and stored with it; an idempotent replay returns the stored intent and never reassigns. The rule is normative so anyone holding the user's secret can recompute it from the database: d = HMAC-SHA256(key = UTF-8 user secret, message = UTF-8 intentId); the low bit of the digest's LAST byte, (d[31] & 1), 1 → "treatment", 0 → "control". Never sent to a merchant. E1 (AGENT_COOKIE_EXPERIMENT=ranking, and only while the installed policy document has non-zero `ranking` weights): treatment gets outcome-aware ranking, control gets today's order and no `ucp.rank` event.

accepted.description: Of those, intents with an accepted quote (an accept that policy blocked is not an accept).

wilson95.description: Wilson score interval for `rate`, z = 1.96, clamped to [0, 1]; [0, 1] when n = 0.

medianAcceptMs.description: Median milliseconds from intent creation to its first accept; absent when nothing was accepted.

ExperimentArmStats.description: One arm of an experiment. Counts only.

ExperimentReport.description: Response of GET /owner/experiments. Computed from the stored arms, so it is reproducible from the database alone. `sample` is true unless the workspace talks to live merchants. No claim about lift belongs anywhere before each arm reaches the minimum n the plan states (docs/commerce-analytics-plan.md §6).

purpose.description: The purpose the read was made under ("" for auto fields).

FieldsResponse.description: GET /agent/fields → 200: the released values. A requested field the user has no value for is absent.

ForgetRequest.description: POST /personal/learned/forget (B49): forget what was learned from one conversation or one intent. Exactly one of the two. Every contribution whose evidence names it is revoked in one SQLite transaction and one memory-repo commit (with CARD.md); a waiting batch of that conversation is dropped, and a learner answer still in flight for it is discarded when it arrives. A later new message in the same conversation is learned from again.

FunnelReport.description: Response of GET /owner/funnel. `sample` is true unless the workspace talks to live merchants.

source.description: "fixture" when any merchant answer for this intent was a recorded replay; "live" otherwise.

introduced.description: Merchants introduced (sessions attached to the intent, every channel).

firstQuoteMs.description: Milliseconds from intent creation to the first quote; absent when nobody quoted.

outcome.description: The accepted quote's terminal status, once there is one.

fieldsGranted.description: Distinct field names in the grants issued for this intent (every merchant).

fieldsRead.description: Distinct field names merchants actually read under those grants. fieldsRead / fieldsGranted is the minimization ratio.

purposeReleases.description: Receipts written for this intent: purpose releases, handshake (auto-field) reads and Tier 0 deliveries.

createdBy.description: Bring-your-own-agent: the agent (personal or assistant) that created the intent; absent on legacy rows.

questionsSkipped.description: Questions the user was not asked: the sum of field names across this intent's receipts (fields served to agents by policy at the stage that needed them). Counts only; it is the plan's measure of "skip onboarding".

arm.description: Phase 4: the holdout arm the intent was assigned at creation (stored with it); absent when no experiment ran.

FunnelRow.description: One intent, from creation to its terminal outcome.

FunnelStage.description: Where an intent is in the buying funnel. Ordered; a session's stage for an intent only moves forward.

fields.description: Fields readable with this grant without a purpose (the category's auto fields).

policyId.description: Additive (Phase 1): id of the policy document the grant was issued under (policy-document.ts policyId).

stage.description: Additive (Phase 2): the funnel stage that issued the grant — "introduced" for the handshake grant; "quoted", "accepted", "checkout", "payment" for grants the workspace opens when the merchant reaches that stage for the intent. A stage grant's purpose is the stage name; the installed document decides which fields it opens.

GrantView.description: One row of GET /personal/grants: the contract Grant plus who holds it and how long it has left. No values.

jar.description: Workspace API base URL. The merchant calls this; no discovery mechanism needed.

Handshake.description: A04 wording: lang / tone / length ARE three values — they say "how to talk to me" and travel with every handshake. "No values in the handshake" means `available` lists field NAMES only; every other value is fetched through GET /agent/fields and checked against policy, grant and purpose at read time.

IntentEvent.description:
One event on GET /personal/intents/:id/events (`text/event-stream`). Each event is one SSE frame:

    event: <IntentEvent.type>     data: <JSON of the IntentEvent>     id: <quote seq>                  (quote events only)

The SSE `id` of a quote frame is that quote's insertion sequence in the workspace: decimal digits, strictly increasing in insertion order, otherwise opaque (gaps are normal). A client that reconnects with `Last-Event-ID: <id>` gets only the quotes inserted after it, then the live ones; `complete` and `expired` frames carry no id, so they never move the resume point. A quote's payload is exactly what GET …/quotes returns for the same quote: no field value beyond it.

 quote    — existing quotes first, in sequence order, then each new quote as it is inserted.  complete — every introduced merchant that can quote (every introduction but Tier 0) has quoted; the same rule             as `complete` on GET …/quotes. The stream closes after it.  expired  — the intent's `expiresAt` passed on the workspace clock; its quotes can no longer be accepted. The             stream closes after it. Checked before `complete`, so an expired intent never reports `complete`.

The workspace also closes a stream INTENT_STREAM_MAX_MS after it opened, and at once on demo reset. A stream that ends without `complete` or `expired` is not an error: resume with Last-Event-ID, or read GET …/quotes. Lines that start with ":" are heartbeat comments, sent every INTENT_STREAM_HEARTBEAT_MS; clients ignore them.

accepted.description: The quote the user accepted for this intent, if any.

IntentHistoryEntry.description: GET /personal/intents?q= — the user's own intent history, newest first.

IntentRequest.description: POST /personal/intents body (2026-10-17, human direction: search is driven by the user's sentence; replaces the fixed trail_shoes / EU 42 / $120 / pinned-store demo).  - text   — the user's own words, verbatim. Required. The UCP query when `query` is absent; the chat message for             Tier 0 merchants. Never sent in introduce callbacks.  - query  — what to search for, when the personal agent extracted it (e.g. English keywords for UCP).  - public — conditions the user stated in THIS request; sent to introduced merchants. Known keys:      budget   USD, "120" / "$120" / "100-160" (upper bound). HARD: offers above it are dropped.      size     e.g. "42", "US 9". SOFT: ranks matching variants first; never excludes. A quote whose variant does               not match carries `sizeNote` ("没有 42，有 41、43"). `shoe_size` is accepted as an alias.      count    how many different sellers to quote, 1–5 (default 2).      color, deadline, … other public conditions, passed through.    Not stated → the card's budget / shoe_size are used to RANK only, never to exclude.  - kind   — optional hint, not an enum: registered merchants listing it in `capabilities` are introduced too.

JwksResponse.description: GET /.well-known/agent-cookie-jwks.json: one key for an existing session while the jar is wired and unlocked, else none.

LearnedEntry.description: GET /personal/learned: every `pref.*` value on the card ("card") or waiting for a second source ("candidate"), with who contributed it and why. RulesApi.mergeCard decides: the user's own statement ("stated") is on the card at once (medium); an observed or inferred value needs two independent sources — two different conversations or intents, not two agents.

models.description: Which models produced a learned contribution (B60). Provenance only, never authority.

LearnedEvidence.description: One piece of evidence behind a learned value, as GET /personal/learned shows it.

sessionId.description: Set on approval: the assistant's pairwise session.

url.description: Where the owner decides: an ABSOLUTE URL of the workspace resource (`${jar}/owner/links/${id}`); a console or gateway renders it.

LinkView.description: Assistant view (POST /assistant/link, GET /assistant/link/:id): never the owner's data, only the state of its own link.

Me.description: Response of GET /me: three strings. An owner key reports category "personal" (it acts for the user) and role "owner".

sessionId.description: The session the fact is about; without it, this merchant's session with the user.

MerchantContributionRequest.description: POST /agent/contributions body. A field outside the policy's write section, or a name outside the field table, is kept as the merchant's own "inferred" record and never reaches the card (A11), so `field` is any name here.

sessions.description: Sessions the merchant holds (pairwise: one per user).

returningSessions.description: Of those, sessions introduced to more than one intent (the user came back).

quotes.description: Quotes the merchant submitted (for a UCP store proxy, the quotes made from its catalog).

accepted.description: Of those, quotes the user accepted (an accept that policy blocked is not counted).

winRate.description: accepted / quotes; 0 when there are no quotes.

medianQuoteMs.description: Median milliseconds from an intent's creation to this merchant's quote for it; absent when there are no quotes.

MerchantStats.description: Response of GET /agent/stats: the calling merchant's own history in this workspace, over its own `agent_id` only. Counts only: no session id, no field name or value, nothing about any other merchant.

NoteView.description: GET /agent/notes/:key: the merchant's own note (anyone else gets 404). Reading it extends its expiry.

conversationId.description: Opaque, chosen by the personal agent; stable across posts of one conversation.

ObservationAck.description: POST /personal/observations → 202. `duplicate`: every turn was a replay (messageId already seen); nothing queued.

at.description: ISO time the turn was said.

messageId.description: Opaque id of the message on its channel (B49, optional). A turn whose messageId the same personal agent already posted within OBSERVATION_MESSAGE_TTL_MS is ignored, so a replay is not a second sighting.

ObservationTurn.description: POST /personal/observations body: turns of a conversation the personal agent took part in or overheard. Only the user's own turns are ever learned from; "agent" and "other" turns are dropped on arrival. Turns are batched per (personal agent, conversationId); Dreaming learns from a batch once it has been quiet for OBSERVATION_IDLE_MS or holds OBSERVATION_BATCH_TURNS turns, never on arrival. The text is held in workspace memory only (B49): at most OBSERVATION_MAX_CONVERSATIONS conversations × OBSERVATION_MAX_QUEUED_TURNS turns, the oldest dropped (and counted in the activity log) past that; SQLite keeps only the conversationId, turn count and times, and a restart loses what was waiting. While learning is paused the observation is discarded.

status.description: `reversed` (additive): the hold was released at the provider because the store did not take the delegated payment (today's UCP adapter passes none to complete), so nothing remains held on the user's card.

value.description: At most 512 UTF-8 bytes. payment_method takes a provider token reference only; never a card number.

PersonalContributionRequest.description: POST /personal/contributions body: one fact the user stated (stored with basis "stated").

auto.description: Readable with the handshake, no purpose needed.

purpose.description: Readable only when the declared purpose is listed.

ranking.description: Phase 3, optional: outcome-aware seller ranking weights. Absent = catalog order after size and preferences.

PolicyDocument.description: v1: today's POLICY.yaml shape. Field order inside the arrays is significant (handshake `available`, Tier 0 prefix).

source.description: "default" = compiled DEFAULT_POLICY; "repo" = POLICY.yaml in the memory repo; "installed" = PUT by the owner, held in SQLite.

PolicyView.description: Response of GET /personal/policy. `source`: where the installed document came from.

PublicJwk.description: A session's pairwise jar public key (lane D): Ed25519, as RFC 8037 OKP.

price.description: Integer, minor units of `currency` (cents): 11995 means $119.95. Same convention as UCP.

etaDate.description: ISO date when the merchant committed to one; null when unknown. Not knowing the arrival date is the normal case (UCP catalog results carry no delivery estimate) — never invent one. Put the merchant's own wording, if any, in `etaText`.

seller.description: seller.domain of the UCP store (the proxy agent's `domain`).

source.description: Set by the workspace on every quote it returns (additive, B20).

sizeNote.description: UCP quotes, when the wanted size (stated in the request, else the card's) is not this variant's: what the store has instead, e.g. "没有 42，有 41、43" / "No 42; has 41, 43". Absent when sizes match or do not apply.

QuotesResponse.description: GET /personal/intents/:id/quotes. `complete`: every introduced merchant that can quote has quoted.

RankStats.description: What moved the order of one search (`ucp.rank` activity event). Ranks are the integer sort buckets, not scores.

RankingWeights.description: Integer weights 0–100 in the policy document (`ranking`). Both 0, or the section absent, means today's order: pinned, size, preferences, budget, catalog order. outcomeRank = −(round(winRate·winRate) − round(failRate·failure)), so sellers with equal history tie and catalog order still breaks the tie.

amount.description: Filled by lane D's payment authorization.

intentId.description: Additive (Phase 0): the intent whose grant authorized the release; absent on legacy rows. Funnel attribution only.

policyId.description: Additive (Phase 1): id of the policy document that allowed this release (policy-document.ts policyId).

capabilities.description: Up to 20 strings of 1–64 characters; a registered merchant listing an intent's `kind` here is introduced to it.

callbackUrl.description: http(s) URL where the workspace POSTs `introduce` and `accepted` callbacks (MerchantCallback). Merchants only.

chatEndpoint.description: Tier 0: http(s) URL of a chat endpoint that receives the handshake as a text prefix. Merchants only.

RegisterRequest.description: POST /agents/register body. A personal agent needs the owner key; an assistant takes no callbackUrl or chatEndpoint.

Registration.description: Response of POST /agents/register. The key is shown once; callers keep it in AGENT_COOKIE_KEY, never in chat or commits.

Role.description: category === "personal" ? "personal" : "merchant" for registered agents. "owner" is the user's own console/CLI key: it alone may call /owner/activity and /demo/reset (/demo/reset additionally requires AGENT_COOKIE_DEMO=1). Owner keys are not tied to a category; the fake workspace maps them from fixtures/dev-keys.json, the real one mints them at seed time.

droppedInvalid.description: Malformed price or missing seller/variant id.

eligibleSellers.description: Distinct seller domains among eligible offers.

SearchStats.description: What the hard filters did to one catalog search (apps/workspace ucp-filter: USD, ships to the user's country, available, the budget stated in this request, the card's learned `pref.avoid`). `offers` = eligible + every dropped bucket; an offer is counted in the first bucket that rejects it, checked in the order avoid, currency, unavailable, shipsTo, invalid price, budget, missing seller or variant id (`invalid`).

unchanged.description: (ref, field) pairs whose decision is the same under both documents.

ShadowReport.description: Response of POST /personal/policy/shadow: every past release (receipt) and every logged field read re-evaluated under a candidate document, compared with the installed one. Ids, field NAMES and decision codes only.

policy.description: The candidate document; it must pass the floor (policyViolations), else 422.

text.description: What the user reads: at most 1000 UTF-8 bytes.

etaDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD (or a full ISO timestamp) only when the merchant commits to a date; null or absent when unknown.

etaText.description: The merchant's own delivery wording, at most 200 bytes.

checkoutUrl.description: https only, no credentials in the URL.

UnlockRequest.description: POST /personal/unlock body (lane D): the unlock app's HMAC handoff token, issued after a passkey assertion.

unlockedUntil.description: Epoch milliseconds until which the jar stays unlocked.

value.description: At most NOTE_MAX_BYTES (2048) UTF-8 bytes; never a card number.
